title: 4. FinTech Landscape
subtitle: 5G · Mobile apps · Cloud · Web 2.0 · AI/ML in fraud detection · API-driven banking
subject: FinTech

sections.heading: 4.1 5G, Mobile Apps and Smartphones
sections.html:
Updated for Assessment Year 2026-27 (income of FY 2025-26, assessed under the Income-tax Act, 1961).

Objectives: understand the technologies powering modern FinTech and open banking.

5G offers ultra-low latency (about 1 ms) and high speed, enabling real-time trading, biometric authentication and IoT payments. Smartphones with biometrics and NFC are the primary banking channel.

sections.heading: 4.2 Transforming Customer Experience
sections.html:
Personalised dashboards, chatbots, video KYC, voice banking and one-tap payments.

Example: HDFC Bank's EVA chatbot answers queries instantly.

sections.heading: 4.3 Cloud Computing
sections.html: On-demand computing with models IaaS, PaaS, SaaS. It offers elasticity and lower capex; RBI requires data localisation of payment data.

sections.heading: 4.4 Web 2.0, Rapid Web Design and JavaScript
sections.html: Web 2.0 introduced interactive, user-generated content. Rapid design uses responsive frameworks (Bootstrap) and prototyping tools. JavaScript (React, Node.js) powers dynamic banking dashboards and real-time updates.

sections.heading: 4.5 AI and Machine Learning in FinTech
sections.html:
Applications: credit scoring, chatbots, algorithmic trading, underwriting. Fraud detection: ML models learn normal behaviour and flag anomalies.

Example: A card used in Chennai at 2 pm and in London at 2:10 pm is flagged and blocked automatically.

sections.heading: 4.6 API-driven Banking
sections.html: An API (Application Programming Interface) lets systems exchange data securely. Benefits: faster integration, new revenue streams, better customer experience. Trends: open banking, Banking-as-a-Service, embedded finance, Account Aggregator framework.
